name: CustomerCreditTransferInitiation
label: Customer Credit Transfer Initiation
summary: A customer instructing its bank to make one or many credit transfers. The front door of the payments chain — what a corporate ERP or treasury system emits.
whenUsed: Payroll runs, supplier payment files, treasury transfers, any batch a corporate sends its bank. The bank validates it, responds with a pain.002, then converts each payment into an interbank pacs.008. One pain.001 file routinely becomes hundreds of pacs.008 messages.
gotchas: Three levels, and the middle one matters. Anything that is shared across a batch — debtor account, execution date, payment method, charge bearer — belongs at PaymentInformation, not repeated per transaction. Files that repeat it per transaction still validate but defeat the structure.

BatchBooking decides what the debtor's statement looks like: true gives one aggregated debit, false gives one entry per payment. Clients reconciling per invoice need false, and discovering this after go-live means reprocessing a month of statements.
RequestedExecutionDate is a request, not a promise. Submit after the cut-off, or on a non-business day, and the bank will move it — so never treat it as the settlement date for forecasting.

fields.name: Message Identification
fields.note: Unique per sending customer. Banks duplicate-check on it, so a resubmitted file needs a new id — this is the most common cause of a whole payroll file being silently ignored.

fields.name: Number Of Transactions
fields.note: Total transactions across all PaymentInformation blocks, not the number of blocks.

fields.name: Control Sum
fields.note: Sum of every instructed amount in the file, currency-agnostic. The cheapest guard against a truncated file — populate it.

fields.name: Initiating Party
fields.note: Who sent the file. Often a shared-service centre or a payment factory, which is not necessarily the debtor on any individual payment.

fields.name: Initiating Party Identification
fields.note: Where the bank-assigned customer or file-sender id goes. Banks commonly require it for entitlement checks.

fields.name: Forwarding Agent
fields.note: An agent relaying the file on the customer's behalf.

fields.name: Payment Information
fields.note: A batch of payments sharing a debtor account, execution date and method. The level most implementations under-use.

fields.name: Payment Information Identification
fields.note: Your reference for this batch. Appears in the pain.002 response, so make it meaningful.

fields.name: Payment Method
fields.note: TRF for credit transfers, CHK for cheques. Fixed for the whole batch.

fields.name: Batch Booking
fields.note: true for a single aggregated debit on the statement, false for one entry per payment. Drives downstream reconciliation; agree it with the bank before go-live.

fields.name: Number Of Transactions
fields.note: Count within this batch only.

fields.name: Payment Type Information
fields.note: Can be set here for the whole batch or per transaction — but not both. Mixing levels is a frequent rejection cause.

fields.name: Service Level Code
fields.note: SEPA for euro area credit transfers, INST for instant rails.

fields.name: Category Purpose Code
fields.note: SALA on a payroll batch is more than documentation — many banks use it to suppress the individual amounts from statements and reports visible to other staff.

fields.name: Requested Execution Date
fields.note: When the debtor wants the batch executed. Mandatory. Newer versions allow a date-time choice; some banks accept only the date form.

fields.name: Debtor
fields.note: Whose account is debited for this whole batch.

fields.name: Debtor Postal Address
fields.note: Use structured elements — the bank will copy whatever you send into the outbound pacs.008, where unstructured addresses are being rejected.

fields.name: Debtor Account
fields.note: Mandatory at this level. One account per PaymentInformation block — paying from two accounts means two blocks.

fields.name: Account Currency
fields.note: Needed to disambiguate a multi-currency account.

fields.name: Debtor Agent
fields.note: The bank being instructed.

fields.name: Charge Bearer
fields.note: Set here for the batch. SLEV for SEPA; DEBT where the corporate wants beneficiaries to receive the full amount.

fields.name: Charges Account
fields.note: Lets fees be debited to a separate account from the payments. Useful for cost-centre accounting.

fields.name: Credit Transfer Transaction Information
fields.note: One per individual payment.

fields.name: Instruction Identification
fields.note: Your reference between you and your bank. Echoed in the pain.002, so this is how you match a rejection back to a row in your own ledger.

fields.name: End To End Identification
fields.note: Travels unchanged to the beneficiary. Put the invoice or payroll reference here — it is what makes the creditor's reconciliation automatic.

fields.name: Payment Type Information
fields.note: Per-payment override. Only valid if the batch level did not set it.

fields.name: Amount
fields.note: A choice: InstdAmt, or EqvtAmt for 'send this much in the beneficiary's currency from my account in mine'.

fields.name: Instructed Amount
fields.note: The normal case. Currency as an attribute.

fields.name: Equivalent Amount
fields.note: Amount in one currency to be paid from an account in another, with the FX left to the bank.

fields.name: Exchange Rate Information
fields.note: Where a pre-agreed rate or contract reference applies.

fields.name: Exchange Rate
fields.note: A rate the debtor is asserting rather than requesting. Only honoured where a deal already exists.

fields.name: Contract Identification
fields.note: Reference of a pre-agreed FX contract, so the bank applies the dealt rate instead of the spot rate. The MT field 21F position.

fields.name: Intermediary Agent 1
fields.note: Only specify routing if you have a genuine reason; banks generally route better than their customers can.

fields.name: Creditor Agent
fields.note: The beneficiary's bank. Optional where the IBAN alone identifies it; required for most non-IBAN countries.

fields.name: Creditor
fields.note: Optional in the schema, required by every bank in practice.

fields.name: Creditor Name
fields.note: Must match the account holder's registered name. Confirmation-of-Payee checks reject on mismatch, and 140 characters is the ceiling.

fields.name: Country
fields.note: Mandatory for cross-border; the single most-missed element in corporate files.

fields.name: Other Account Identification
fields.note: For Australia, BSB and account number concatenated, or split using the proprietary scheme name — check your bank's guide, as practice differs.

fields.name: Instruction For Debtor Agent
fields.note: Free text for your own bank. Usually requires a bilateral agreement to be acted on rather than ignored.

fields.name: Regulatory Reporting
fields.note: Required for cross-border payments in jurisdictions with exchange-control reporting.

fields.name: Unstructured Remittance Information
fields.note: 140 characters per occurrence, and most rails will forward only the first one.

fields.name: Structured Remittance Information
fields.note: Proper invoice-level detail. The right answer for payables, where supported.
